Table 25.2 Risk Factors for Osteoporosis 
Fracture
Major Risk Factors
j
• Low bone mineral density
• Personal history of fracture as an adult
• History of fracture in a parent or sibling
• Female sex
• Age 65 years or older
• Caucasian race
• Menopause before age 45 years
• Premenopausal amenorrhea for 1 year or more
• Glucocorticoid therapy for >3 months
• Recurrent falls
Minor Risk Factors
• Impaired vision
• Dementia
• Alcoholism
• Low lifelong calcium and vitamin D intake
• Physical inactivity
• Poor health/frailty
• Current cigarette smoking
• Body weight <127 lb (<58 kg)
